questions.question: What is the basic unit of life?
questions.explanation: All living things are made of cells. Cells are the smallest unit that can carry out life processes.
questions.funFact: The human body contains about 37 trillion cells — that's more cells than stars in the Milky Way!

questions.question: What organelle is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria convert glucose and oxygen into ATP (energy) through cellular respiration.
questions.funFact: Mitochondria have their own DNA, suggesting they were once free-living bacteria that were absorbed by larger cells billions of years ago!

questions.question: What is the process by which plants make their own food using sunlight?
questions.explanation: During photosynthesis, plants use sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide to produce glucose and oxygen.
questions.funFact: If all the plants on Earth stopped photosynthesis for just one year, most life on the planet would die from lack of oxygen and food!

questions.question: In Newton's First Law, what does an object at rest tend to do?
questions.explanation: Newton's First Law (inertia) states that an object at rest stays at rest unless acted on by an unbalanced external force.
questions.funFact: Inertia is why you jerk forward when a car brakes suddenly — your body wants to keep moving even after the car stops!

questions.question: What are the three states of matter?
questions.explanation: Matter exists as solid (fixed shape), liquid (fixed volume), or gas (no fixed shape or volume).
questions.funFact: Plasma is actually a fourth state of matter — it makes up over 99% of the visible universe, including the Sun!

questions.question: What type of rock is formed when molten lava cools and solidifies?
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form when magma (underground) or lava (above ground) cools and hardens.
questions.funFact: The word 'igneous' comes from the Latin word 'ignis', meaning fire. Obsidian, a natural glass used as arrowheads, is an igneous rock!

questions.question: What is the chemical formula for water?
questions.explanation: Water is made of two hydrogen atoms bonded to one oxygen atom (H2O).
questions.funFact: Water is the only substance on Earth that naturally exists in all three states — solid ice, liquid water, and water vapor — at everyday temperatures!

questions.question: In the food chain, what are organisms called that make their own food?
questions.explanation: Producers (like plants and algae) use photosynthesis to create their own food from sunlight, forming the base of every food chain.
questions.funFact: Ocean phytoplankton (tiny producers) generate over 50% of the Earth's oxygen supply — more than all land forests combined!

questions.question: What layer of the Earth is the thickest?
questions.explanation: The mantle is approximately 2,900 km thick and makes up about 84% of Earth's total volume.
questions.funFact: The mantle is solid rock, but it flows very slowly over millions of years — like extremely thick silly putty — which moves the tectonic plates above it!

questions.question: What gas makes up the largest percentage of Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere. Oxygen is second at about 21%.
questions.funFact: Although we breathe nitrogen constantly, our bodies cannot use it directly. Certain bacteria in soil 'fix' nitrogen into a form that plants — and ultimately we — can use!

questions.question: What is the term for a push or pull that can change an object's motion?
questions.explanation: A force is any push or pull. Forces can start motion, stop motion, or change the direction of a moving object.
questions.funFact: The four fundamental forces of nature are gravity, electromagnetism, the strong nuclear force, and the weak nuclear force. All everyday forces are combinations of these!

questions.question: Which part of a cell contains the genetic information (DNA)?
questions.explanation: The nucleus acts as the cell's control center, housing the DNA that carries instructions for every function the cell performs.
questions.funFact: If you uncoiled and stretched out all the DNA from a single human cell, it would be about 2 meters (6.5 feet) long — yet it fits inside a nucleus smaller than a grain of sand!

questions.question: What is the speed of light in a vacuum?
questions.explanation: Light travels at approximately 300,000 kilometers per second (186,000 miles per second) in a vacuum.
questions.funFact: Light from the Sun takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth. When you look at the Sun, you're actually seeing what it looked like 8 minutes ago!

questions.question: What kind of energy does a moving object have?
questions.explanation: Kinetic energy is the energy of motion. The faster an object moves and the more mass it has, the more kinetic energy it possesses.
questions.funFact: A professional baseball pitched at 100 mph has enough kinetic energy that if it were fully converted to heat, it could raise the temperature of a small cup of water by about 1 degree!

questions.question: What is the process of water turning from liquid to vapor called?
questions.explanation: Evaporation occurs when water molecules at the surface gain enough energy to escape into the air as water vapor.
questions.funFact: Sweating cools you down because of evaporation — when sweat evaporates from your skin, it carries heat away with it!

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a renewable energy source?
questions.explanation: Coal is a fossil fuel formed over millions of years and cannot be replenished on a human timescale, making it non-renewable.
questions.funFact: The coal we burn today was formed from the remains of forests that existed over 300 million years ago — long before the dinosaurs!

questions.question: What is the name for the movement of tectonic plates that causes earthquakes and volcanoes?
questions.explanation: Plate tectonics describes how Earth's outer shell is divided into several plates that glide over the mantle, causing geological events at their boundaries.
questions.funFact: The plates move at about the same speed your fingernails grow — only a few centimeters per year. But over millions of years, this has rearranged all the continents!

questions.question: What is the role of decomposers in an ecosystem?
questions.explanation: Decomposers (fungi and bacteria) break down dead plants and animals into simpler substances, recycling nutrients back into the soil.
questions.funFact: A single teaspoon of healthy forest soil can contain more bacteria than there are people on Earth!

questions.question: In a longitudinal wave, what moves parallel to the direction of wave travel?
questions.explanation: In a longitudinal wave like sound, particles are compressed and spread out (rarefied) in the same direction the wave travels.
questions.funFact: Sound cannot travel through the vacuum of space because there are no particles to compress. Space battles in movies with sound effects are scientifically impossible!

questions.question: What is the term for the transfer of heat by direct contact between objects?
questions.explanation: Conduction transfers heat through direct contact. Metal is an excellent conductor because its electrons can move freely and carry energy.
questions.funFact: Metal feels colder than wood at the same temperature because metal conducts heat away from your hand faster, tricking your nerves into sensing cold!
